To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of the World-Wide Web is perceived as being high when it is used to perform a travel task, when users are less uncertain about the task, when the World-Wide-Web is perceived as an important information resource, and when users are more satisfied with the Web as an interface.
the task-technology model is a good model for the evaluation of the World WideWeb as a resource.

the performance of the World wide Web as an information source is perceived to be high and the performance of the Web as a travel information source is perceived as higher than the performance of the Internet as a whole.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of the WorldWideWeb as an information resource and the role of uncertainty in explaining perceived performance.
the evaluation of the Web as an electronic information resource and the development of a richer model of usage.
the performance of the Web as a resource for travel information, but the findings are applicable to other domains and tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the World Wide Web can be considered a successful information resource, but that this success is moderated by the task-technology match, the degree of uncertainty reduction and the mediation of the World Wide Wide Web.
the Web has the potential to be an information resource for travel tasks, but the extent to which this potential is realised is dependent on the extent to which the task-technology match is achieved.

perceived performance of the Web as an Information Resource (PIR) is determined by the interaction of a number of factors, including the task being performed, the level of uncertainty, the level of mediation of the task and the level of information-seeking behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the task-technology-fit model and the uncertainty construct are useful for explaining perceived performance of the Web as an informational resource.

a richer model is needed that takes into account the broader context of World Wide web usage, the role of uncertainty reduction in the information-seeking process, the role of information resources, and the impact of the World Wide web as an information resource.
the World Wide Web has become a very important information resource in the travel domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a richer model of information systems success is required to explain usage of the Web as an informational resource.
the Web is not an all-encompassing resource.
a richer theoretical model that includes the construct of uncertainty is needed to explain the perceived performance of the Web.
